summary: Updates RFC 5480 to specify what the keyEncipherment and dataEncipherment key usage bits mean in certificates that support elliptic curve cryptography.

plainLanguage.summary: Certificates use key usage values to state what a public key is for. RFC 8813 clarifies that two values, keyEncipherment and dataEncipherment, must not appear for three specified elliptic-curve public key identifiers.

questions: what does keyencipherment mean for ecc certificates
what does rfc 8813 change in rfc 5480
which key usage values are prohibited for ecc certificates
subtitle: Clarifies two key usage values for certificates using elliptic-curve algorithms.

tldr.problem: RFC 5480 specified seven of the nine key usage values for elliptic-curve certificates but did not address keyEncipherment or dataEncipherment.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 8813 updates Section 3 of RFC 5480: when keyUsage is present for the covered key identifiers, keyEncipherment and dataEncipherment MUST NOT be present.
tldr.outcome: RFC 8813 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 5480 with explicit rules for the two omitted key usage bits.

today: RFC 8813 is a Proposed Standard from August 2020 and updates RFC 5480.

sections.title: The Missing Key Usage Rules
sections.content:
RFC 5480 defines the Subject Public Key Information field for certificates that support Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC). It also specifies permissible combinations of values in the keyUsage extension, but does not mention the keyEncipherment and dataEncipherment bits.

RFC 8813 updates the end of Section 3 of RFC 5480 to state the rules for those values.
sections.plainLanguage: The earlier certificate rules omitted two key usage values. This update says when those values cannot be used with the covered ECC keys.

sections.title: The Two Prohibited Values
sections.content:
If a certificate has a keyUsage extension and its SubjectPublicKeyInfo indicates id-ecPublicKey, then keyEncipherment and dataEncipherment MUST NOT be present.

The same two values MUST NOT be present when the SubjectPublicKeyInfo indicates id-ecDH or id-ecMQV. The prohibition applies when the keyUsage extension is present.
sections.plainLanguage: When keyUsage is present, certificates for id-ecPublicKey, id-ecDH, or id-ecMQV cannot include keyEncipherment or dataEncipherment.

sections.title: Security and IANA
sections.content: The RFC introduces no new security considerations beyond those in RFC 5480. It also states that it has no IANA actions.
sections.plainLanguage: This update adds no new security considerations and requires no IANA changes.
